statement.p: The graphs of functions f and g are shown below.
Use interval notation in your answers. Use inf to represent infinity.

solution.p: The question f(x) \gt g(x) is asking: For what x values, are function fs y values greater than function gs y values? We can break down this question into two steps:

li.p: In the graph, identify the part(s) where function fs y values are greater than function gs y values.
Identify the x values corresponding to that part(s).

solution.p: The following graph identifies the part which satisfies f(x) \gt g(x).
The corresponding x values in the graph are in {\left(-\infty ,3\right)}. In other words, to satisfy f(x) \gt g(x), the x values need to be in {\left(-\infty ,3\right)}.
Similarly, in the other part(s) of the graph, function fs y values are smaller than or equal to function gs y values. To satisfy f(x) \le g(x), the x values need to be in {\left[3,\infty \right)}.
